newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Papoutsis encouraged by debate on renewable energy.
newsitem.headline: Papoutsis encouraged by debate on renewable energy.

text.p: Energy Commissioner Christos Papoutsis said he was encouraged on Tuesday by support shown for the Commission's proposals in a debate among EU energy ministers on the use of renewable energy sources.
The Energy Council discussed the Commission's green paper on renewable energy sources which was adopted last month.

The Commission called for the use of renewable energy sources to be doubled to 12 percent of total energy consumption by 2010, partly because of environmental reasons and to cut dependency on imported fuels.
Papoutsis said there had been "great support" shown for the Commission's strategy. "This is a very encouraging message," he told a news conference.
He said he hoped the Commission would next year present a white paper on the issue as well as an action plan.
In the debate, ministers stressed the importance for the EU to develop policies for a renewable energy resources strategy.
They agreed that the share of renewable energy should be increased but some questioned the need for quantitative targets.
